# ‘The Love Guru,’ Paris Hilton dominate 29th Razzie Awards

**LOS ANGELES —** Hollywood celebrated its worst Saturday night, as Mike Myers’ critically panned comedy “The Love Guru” and celebrity heiress Paris Hilton led the winners at the 29th Annual Golden Raspberry Awards.

Held February 21, 2009 — one night before the Academy Awards — the Razzies handed “The Love Guru” three of their spray-painted trophies: worst picture, worst actor for Myers and worst screenplay.

Razzie founder John Wilson described the film as “the entertainment equivalent of someone passing gas at a dinner party,” adding that Myers had taken a character that “nobody liked” and stretched it into a feature-length movie.

Hilton also collected three awards. She was named worst actress for “The Hottie & the Nottie,” worst supporting actress for the horror musical “Repo! The Genetic Opera,” and shared worst screen couple for “The Hottie & the Nottie” with either of her co-stars, Christine Lakin or Joel David Moore.

Wilson was blunt about Hilton’s screen work, saying she “couldn’t act her way out of a paper bag.”

Pierce Brosnan received the worst supporting actor award for his singing performance in the hit musical “Mamma Mia!” The night’s worst prequel, remake, rip-off or sequel honor went to “Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull.”

German filmmaker Uwe Boll was named worst director for three films — “In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale,” “1968 Tunnel Rats” and “Postal.” He also received a special worst career achievement award, with the Razzies labeling him “Germany’s answer to Ed Wood.”

Boll participated through a prerecorded video in which he joked about his reputation and appeared to embrace the dishonor.

The tongue-in-cheek ceremony took place at the Barnsdall Gallery Theatre in Hollywood and featured parody songs, deliberately low-budget production numbers and performers lampooning the year’s most notorious movies. Winners received the traditional Golden Raspberry trophy, a plastic raspberry mounted on a Super 8 film reel and spray-painted gold, valued at less than $5.

The awards were determined by Golden Raspberry Award Foundation members in the United States and abroad. As usual, most of the winners did not attend.

### Major winners

- **Worst Picture:** “The Love Guru”  
- **Worst Actor:** Mike Myers, “The Love Guru”  
- **Worst Actress:** Paris Hilton, “The Hottie & the Nottie”  
- **Worst Supporting Actor:** Pierce Brosnan, “Mamma Mia!”  
- **Worst Supporting Actress:** Paris Hilton, “Repo! The Genetic Opera”  
- **Worst Screen Couple:** Paris Hilton and either Christine Lakin or Joel David Moore, “The Hottie & the Nottie”  
- **Worst Director:** Uwe Boll  
- **Worst Screenplay:** “The Love Guru”  
- **Worst Prequel, Remake, Rip-off or Sequel:** “Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull”  
- **Worst Career Achievement:** Uwe Boll  

The Razzies were created in 1980 by Wilson as a comic counterpoint to awards-season glamour. Nearly three decades later, the ceremony remained committed to its founding mission: reminding Hollywood that not every movie released during the year deserves a gold statue.

In the film, Myers played Guru Pitka, an American raised in India who is hired to repair the marriage of a hockey star. Hilton also won worst supporting actress for her role in the horror musical *Repo! The Genetic Opera*. Her third prize came in the worst screen couple category, shared with either of her co-stars in *The Hottie and the Nottie*, Christine Lakin or Joel David Moore.

The three awards placed Hilton among the most heavily “honored” performers in Razzie history and capped a difficult year for her movie career. *The Hottie and the Nottie* received exceptionally poor reviews and earned only a small theatrical return.

German filmmaker Uwe Boll received two distinctions. He was named worst director for three 2008 releases — *In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale*, *1968: Tunnel Rats* and *Postal* — and was presented with a special worst career achievement award.

Razzie organizers described Boll as “Germany’s answer to Ed Wood,” invoking the cult filmmaker long associated with notoriously low-budget and poorly reviewed movies. Boll built his career largely by adapting video games, including *House of the Dead*, *Alone in the Dark* and *BloodRayne*. His films were routinely attacked by critics but developed a degree of notoriety among fans of cinematic misfires.

The career award was only the third of its kind in Razzie history, underscoring the organizers’ view that Boll’s body of work represented an unusually sustained contribution to bad filmmaking.

Held at the Barnsdall Gallery Theatre one night before the Academy Awards, the annual low-budget ceremony skewered the films, performances and careers that Razzie voters considered 2008’s most regrettable.

Mike Myers’ critically battered comedy *The Love Guru* was named worst picture and also collected awards for worst actor and worst screenplay. Hilton emerged as the evening’s most decorated target, winning worst actress for *The Hottie & the Nottie*, worst supporting actress for *Repo! The Genetic Opera* and worst screen couple for her pairing with either Christine Lakin or Joel David Moore in *The Hottie & the Nottie*.

Neither Myers nor Hilton attended to collect their gold-painted, golf-ball-sized trophies.

## Blockbusters not spared

Commercial success offered no protection from Razzie voters.

*Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull*, which earned more than $790 million worldwide, was named worst prequel, remake, rip-off or sequel. The award reflected the backlash surrounding the long-awaited fourth Indiana Jones adventure, including complaints about its digital effects and much-mocked science-fiction finale.

German filmmaker Uwe Boll was named worst director for *In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale*, *1968 Tunnel Rats* and *Postal*. He also received a special worst career achievement award, with organizers comparing his output to an ongoing assault on cinema.

## Cheap props and expensive flops

As usual, the ceremony presented itself as the anti-Oscars: deliberately shabby, heavy on groan-inducing puns and built around the contrast between Hollywood’s enormous budgets and the Razzies’ reportedly inexpensive trophies.

Presenters joked that *The Love Guru* had achieved spiritual enlightenment by making audiences disappear, while Hilton’s three-award sweep supplied material about fame being easier to obtain than favorable reviews. The Razzies also acknowledged a broader truth about bad-movie history: Financial performance and artistic reputation do not always move together. Some of the night’s targets were outright flops, but others — particularly *Indiana Jones* and *Mamma Mia!* — were among the year’s biggest global hits.

- **Worst picture:** *The Love Guru*

# Paris Hilton and Mike Myers Come Out “On Top—or Bottom” at the Razzies

Paris Hilton and Mike Myers were the biggest losers—and therefore the biggest winners—at the 29th annual Golden Raspberry Awards, Hollywood’s traditional pre-Oscar celebration of the year’s least-admired films.

Hilton swept all three categories in which she was nominated. She was named **Worst Actress** for *The Hottie and the Nottie*, **Worst Supporting Actress** for *Repo! The Genetic Opera*, and shared **Worst Screen Couple** with either Christine Lakin or Joel David Moore for *The Hottie and the Nottie*. Her three-award haul matched Eddie Murphy’s Razzie sweep the previous year.

Myers’ comedy *The Love Guru* took **Worst Picture**, while Myers was voted **Worst Actor** and shared **Worst Screenplay** honors with co-writer Graham Gordy.

Razzie founder John Wilson described the film as “**an entertainment-free 90 minutes**” and joked that it had managed to offend “**Hindus, Canadians and the entire English-speaking world**.”

The remaining major winners were:

- **Worst Supporting Actor:** Pierce Brosnan, *Mamma Mia!*

- **Worst Career Achievement:** Uwe Boll, billed by the Razzies as “**Germany’s answer to Ed Wood**”

Boll embraced the abuse in a recorded acceptance message, calling the Razzies “**the most important awards in Hollywood**” and declaring: “**Everybody can win an Oscar, but only very special people can get a Razzie.**”
